posts.text:
Basic Tenets for Strength from Pavel Tsatsouline:

“Strength is the mother quality of all physical qualities.” 

“Strength is a skill, and, as such, it must be practiced.” 

“Lift heavy, not hard.”

“Anything more than 5 reps is bodybuilding. . . . If you want to be strong, you want to keep your reps at 5 and under.”

“If you are training for strength, you want to try and avoid the burn altogether. The burn is your enemy.”

“Training is something that should be enjoyed.” 

The last quote isn’t a motivational throwaway line. It’s literal. If you’re training for maximal strength, you should feel better after your workout than you did when you walked in. There is a huge neural component.

$ccj $cco remember the eager and aggressive contracting they did at the start of the bull market.  (2020) They wrote in the md&a of expectations of 2% inflation for the next decade? 

Here we are 6 years later with negligible earnings.  The entire Uranium complex contracts ridiculously… some are getting better but long way to go.  

Everyone must also not just fact in expectations for rising operating costs.  They must truly consider the finding and developing costs that go hand and hand with the huge difficulties to explore and permit uranium assets. 

Show me a company that rushed into production be it a new mine or restart and I’ll show you a company who took extremely valuable in ground resources and threw them away at a fat loss when all in replacement costs are considered.  

This goes for lots of mining companies.  They are so good at destroying shareholder value.
